title: Surging Demand: Data Center Direct-to-Chip Cooling Market Poised for 26.5% CAGR Growth by 2032
author: Researchandmarkets.Com
description: The data center direct-to-chip cooling market is expected to grow from $3.33 billion in 2026 to $17.31 billion by 2032, driven by increasing demand for thermal management in AI and hyperscale computing. Single-phase systems and water-glycol coolants dominate the market, with hyperscale data centers leading adoption due to energy efficiency and sustainability goals.

title: Why Modine Manufacturing Stock Is Rocketing Higher Today
author: Josh Kohn-Lindquist
description: Modine Manufacturing announced a major $4 billion deal with a hyperscale data center customer for cooling solutions spanning 2027-2029, including a $165 million upfront payment. The deal, representing approximately $1.3 billion in annual revenue starting 2027, significantly exceeds the company's 2025 data center sales of $700 million. With a planned spinoff of its lower-margin performance technologies unit by Q4 2026, Modine is positioned to become a pure-play growth stock focused on data center cooling amid the ongoing AI infrastructure boom.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company secured a landmark $4 billion multi-year contract with a major hyperscaler customer, demonstrating market leadership in data center cooling solutions. The deal validates the company's long-term strategy and positions it for significant revenue growth in the high-margin data center segment. The stock surged 16.8% on the announcement, reflecting strong market confidence in the company's future prospects as it transitions to a pure-play growth company.

title: You Just Missed The SanDisk And Micron Memory Trade: These 10 Stocks Could Ride The Next AI Wave

description: As memory stocks like Micron and SanDisk have already surged dramatically, investors are shifting focus to liquid cooling infrastructure for AI data centers. title: Oil Over $100, a War in the Middle East, and the Fed on Hold. Here's How to Protect Your Artificial Intelligence (AI) Portfolio in 2026.
author: Micah Zimmerman
description: With oil prices surging past $100 due to Middle East tensions and the Fed holding rates steady, AI investors should shift focus from speculative growth stocks to physical infrastructure plays. The article recommends prioritizing companies with contracted capacity, zero debt, and physical assets over software-dependent or highly leveraged positions that are vulnerable to sustained high interest rates and energy costs.
